title: Grade 4 Social Studies — Reading the Geography of the United States
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on states, boundaries, regions, rivers, Great Lakes.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Which Great Lake borders Ohio?
Which river forms much of Ohio's southern boundary?
Which ocean lies along the East Coast of the contiguous United States?
Which ocean lies along the West Coast of the contiguous United States?
Which country lies directly north of the contiguous U.S. along much of its border?
Which country lies directly south of California and Arizona?
Which mountain range includes many high peaks in Colorado?
Which mountain system runs through much of the eastern U.S.?
Which river reaches the Gulf of Mexico south of New Orleans?
Which is a chain of islands in the central Pacific and a U.S. state?
Which U.S. state is separated from the contiguous U.S. by Canada?
Which region includes Ohio under the U.S. Census regional grouping?
Which region lies largely east of the Rocky Mountains and includes broad grasslands?
What can the Great Lakes help nearby cities do?
choices: move into the Atlantic without connecting waterways

questions.question: Which map feature would help compare the elevation of Ohio and Colorado?
choices: a color key showing heights above sea level

questions.question: A ship travels down the Ohio River and reaches the Mississippi. In what general direction does it go downstream from the Ohio's junction?
Why do maps often put Alaska and Hawaii in separate boxes?
choices: They are far from the contiguous states.
They became countries of their own.
They have exactly the same size.
Their names cannot fit on a map.

questions.question: Which is an example of a physical border feature?
choices: a river that follows part of a state boundary

questions.question: Which group consists only of Great Lakes?
Why is it useful to compare two maps of the same U.S. region, one physical and one political?
choices: It tells what each resident thinks.
It shows what the weather will be next month.
Both maps must show exactly the same details.
You can see natural features and how governments divide the land.
